title: Lorentz Rail Sled Tour
description: Guided walkthrough of the drive current, the bench field, the Lorentz force, and the motion it produces.

steps.title: A rail motor, not a railgun
steps.body: Two rails, a sliding armature, and a low-voltage bench supply. Everything you see here is the classroom Lorentz force F = I ℓ × B — there is no projectile, no muzzle energy, and no ballistics anywhere in this model.

steps.title: Step 1 — the drive current
steps.body: The supply pushes current out along one rail, across the armature, and back along the other. The loop is a series R–L circuit: raise the drive slider and watch armature current climb toward V/R.

steps.title: Step 2 — the transverse field
steps.body: The pole pieces above and below the track set a transverse field B across the rails. Move the B slider: this is a local bench parameter, not a live reading from the Halbach or MHD devices.

steps.title: Step 3 — F = I ℓ × B
steps.body: Current I crossing a rail gap ℓ in field B feels a force F = I ℓ B along the track. Halve the field and the force halves with it — the force telemetry follows the product, not either factor alone.

steps.title: Step 4 — motion, friction, and back-EMF
steps.body: The sled accelerates until friction and its own back-EMF (B ℓ v, which subtracts from the supply and cuts the current) balance the drive. Speed levels off well below anything a real launcher would reach — that terminal balance is the point of the demo.

steps.title: What this model is not
steps.body: Lumped circuit plus rigid body: no field solver, no rail erosion, no contact physics, no projectile. Reported position wraps at the end of the 2 m track so the bench reads as a loop. Educational Lorentz force only — not a railgun design tool.
